clue.text: Electronic elements on underside of faux cream pottery

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on the underside of something puts these letters below it
faux means false or fake, so the letters of the word cream are rearranged

parts.note: ICs are integrated circuits, the elements of electronic devices

explanation.surface: A ceramic piece sits on wiring beneath a fake-cream glaze, an odd blend of electronics and craft pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faux' rearranges CREAM into CERAM; in this down entry ICS goes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics is the art and product of fired clay ware, a general name for pottery.

clue.text: See 23
Royal venue in which watch chain is presented to husband with everything

parts.note: an albert is a style of watch chain, named after Prince Albert
all means everything

explanation.surface: At a grand royal venue a man is presented with a watch chain and the whole lot besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Albert Hall is London's famous concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The concert hall in Kensington carries the title Royal, so it is a royal venue.

clue.text: Scoffing second cereal and bulging almost

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: something bulging is full

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs down a second bowl of cereal until nearly bursting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' looks like eating greedily, but the definition takes it as mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock, so scoffing describes a contemptuous, derisive attitude.

clue.text: Nap taken by motorist — quite a blow

parts.note: the nap of a carpet or fabric is its pile
a motorist is a driver

explanation.surface: A motorist takes a nap at the wheel, and it turns out to be quite a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A piledriver is a powerful, crushing punch or kick, so figuratively a mighty blow.

clue.text: Start hoarding Chilean capital like gold dust

indicators.note: hoarding means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a start is a sudden fright, a scare

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone begins stockpiling Chilean money as though it were gold dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' is a noun here: a jolt of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Things described as like gold dust are rare and hard to find, i.e. in short supply.

clue.text: Irony of lake's contribution to climate change?

indicators.note: change tells us these letters are to be altered into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Is a lake's part in global warming an irony?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irony' reads as sarcasm but means iron-like; L from lake joins CLIMATE, and 'change' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony in the literal sense of like iron describes a metal quality.

clue.text: Place for making alcohol from fish covered in blubber

indicators.note: covered in places one piece inside another, the outer one wrapping it

parts.note: to blubber is to cry
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A distillery uses fish wrapped in whale blubber to make its liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cidery is a place where apple juice is fermented into an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Settle for about 50"

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
50 is L in Roman numerals and the mark " stands for an inch

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to accept roughly fifty inches.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle it conclusively.

clue.text: See 3
Red Line Brewery's exceptional drink

indicators.note: exceptional, i.e. out of the ordinary, suggests these letters set out in unusual order

explanation.surface: A brewery called Red Line produces an exceptional beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit-based homemade wine is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Detective said: 'Rubbish order!'

indicators.note: said means spoken, so only the pronunciation of the word counts

parts.note: dick is slang for a private detective
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A detective announces that some command is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consent: an order.

clue.text: Craft a bit of poetry for a beginner

parts.note: a tender is a small boat, a craft serving a larger ship
a foot is a metrical unit, a small piece of verse

explanation.surface: Writing some verse for a novice poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or novice, inexperienced in rough conditions.

clue.text: Note preceding Martin Luther?

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
former means preceding or earlier

explanation.surface: A note pinned up ahead of Martin Luther, perhaps the Wittenberg theses.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation; the question mark signals he is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Luther is the classic example of a religious campaigner who sought to change the Church.

clue.text: Reason to speak about Charlie

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: to say is to speak
a charlie is British slang for a fool, a nit

explanation.surface: A cause to talk regarding someone called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of soundness of mind matches mental health and good sense.

clue.text: Even reading up about desert shows recklessness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
in a down clue, reading up means the letters run backwards

parts.note: even, as in even more, can mean yet
a desert, as in just deserts, is what one merits

explanation.surface: Studying up on the desert can still reveal rash behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: YET written upward gives TEY, which goes 'about' MERIT; 'desert' is the noun from 'deserve', not sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is rash boldness, a disregard of danger that amounts to recklessness.

clue.text: Dukes wear grand poppets

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
poppets and loves are both affectionate terms for dear ones

explanation.surface: Aristocrats dress up their fine little darlings.
explanation.walkthrough: Dukes are fists, from rhyming slang Duke of York(s) for forks, i.e. hands; not noblemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands, slangily called dukes, are covered by these when the weather is cold.

clue.text: It's played using fingers in set order with style

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so these letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: a way is a manner or style

explanation.surface: A pianist runs fingers through a set in the right order and with style.
explanation.definitionFit: A Steinway is a famous make of piano, an instrument played with the fingers.

clue.text: God's city, once a star's retreat

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A deity's former town was once the hideaway of a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star's retreat' turns SUN backwards to NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Uranus was the primordial deity of the sky.

clue.text: One audibly scared of singular substitute for milk

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
creamer is a non-dairy powder used in place of milk in coffee

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened of a single sachet of milk substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who shrieks in fright is noisily expressing fear, so loud fear sums them up.

clue.text: Rough, getting caught having a taste of ale

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ale flavoured with hops tastes hoppy

explanation.surface: A drinker caught sampling ale has a rough time of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppy describes rough water broken up by short, irregular waves.

clue.text: Sarcastic communication that was and is painful to get over

parts.note: barbed remarks are cutting or sarcastic
a wire was a telegram, a dated form of communication

explanation.surface: A cutting old message that still hurts to get past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get over' is literal: climbing over a spiky fence, not recovering from hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiked fencing is painful to climb across, which is its whole purpose.

clue.text: Maybe Paul's articulated vehicle

indicators.note: articulated means spoken aloud, so this is about the sound only

parts.note: Paul McCartney is one of the Fab Four, the band from Liverpool

explanation.surface: Perhaps Paul owns an articulated lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated vehicle' suggests a lorry; 'articulated' is the homophone signal instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen Beetle is a classic small car.

clue.text: Hi-tec group discussion bears fruit on visit

parts.note: Conference is a popular variety of pear
to pay a call is to visit

explanation.surface: A video meeting is going well, the fruit of a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone or video meeting of several people at once is a technological group discussion.

clue.text: See 11
See 22 across
Remove reason for being inside out, maybe

parts.note: up can mean out, as in time is up, or out of bed
the root of something is its source or reason for being

explanation.surface: Taking away someone's purpose for being locked up, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something out by its roots is to remove it entirely.

clue.text: Fancy urinal is of a certain period

indicators.note: fancy, meaning elaborate or ornamented, signals these letters made into something new

explanation.surface: An ornate public toilet is said to date from a particular era.
explanation.definitionFit: The Silurian is a geological period of the Palaeozoic era, so the adjective places something in that time.
